# #2047: Patch: spec check resolves the `§`, `R` and card references inside a ruling's `cards:` line
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Every ruling note carries a `cards:` line naming the cards, spec sections and other rulings it touches — the field a reader browses when asking "what does this ruling affect?". Today a typo there — a wrong ruling number, a renumbered section — rots silently forever. After this patch the repository's own spec checker flags it, the same way it already flags dead references in the notes' bodies and in code.

## Why

`unfilled_fields` (`crates/tools/src/spec.rs:245-251`) verifies `cards:` and `title` are non-empty only; the structured references inside `cards:` are never resolved. Real values cite them: `spec/rulings/R923003.md` has `cards: "§9.9, R97, R923000"`, `R831016.md` has `"Classic #53; §10.6, R99, R177"`, `R910000.md` lists nine card ids. The resolution machinery already exists — `ruling_number` (spec.rs:278), `section_ids` (spec.rs:976-995), the catalog `ids` map (spec.rs:1005) — it is just never run on this field. Citation scanning today covers only code roots (`CITING_ROOTS`, spec.rs:82) and `[[…]]` links (rule 4, spec.rs:1122-1138).

## Proposal

Extend spec check: extract `R<digits>`, `§<n.n>` and card references (`<Set> #<n>` forms, catalog ids) from each note's `cards:` field and resolve them against the existing maps. Free-form tokens that are not references ("B47", "CLAUDE.md rule 4", ranges like `R58–R75`) get a small explicit allowlist. Fix in the same PR any dead references the new rule exposes, and report what it found.

## Where it lands

`crates/tools/src/spec.rs`, plus front-matter fixes in `spec/rulings/*.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` fails on a `cards:` entry naming a nonexistent ruling, section or card
- [ ] It is clean on the committed tree after the PR's fixes
- [ ] `cargo jackioh spec index` output is unchanged apart from the fixes

## Size and risks

Small-medium: one checker rule plus front-matter fixes. The work is a first pass over the ~1,900 `cards:` values to settle which free-form shapes the allowlist needs; a handful of entries may name things that legitimately resolve nowhere and must be reworded rather than whitelisted.
